request.idea: A 9-minute video about building OpenClaw specialist agents that turn vague ideas into finished workflows
constraints: no credentials or tokens in the package
request.sourceNotes: A specialist agent is just a scoped role plus a playbook the agent has to read every run. The failure mode is starting from a blank prompt each time, which produces a different shape of output every run. The fix is a checked-in playbook file that the agent parses at runtime, so the standard and the output cannot drift apart. Once the playbook exists, the agent's job shrinks to judgment: the structure is guaranteed by the file, so the model spends its attention on the parts that actually need taste.

recommended.rationale: Angle: outcome. Front-loads "Turn Vague Ideas", which is the specific thing solo founders and automation builders are searching for. 40 characters, so it survives mobile truncation. Keeps the requested no-hype register: no caps, no exclamation, no promise beyond the video.

thumbnails.name: Face-led: the person mid-decision
thumbnails.layout: Subject on the right third, shot from chest up, looking slightly off-camera toward the text. Text block stacked left, upper two-thirds, nothing in the bottom-right (timestamp overlay lands there).
thumbnails.subject: A single person at a desk mid-work on OpenClaw agents, screen glow on one side of the face, hands visible.
thumbnails.emotion: Focused and slightly amused — a person who just figured something out, not a person shouting.
thumbnails.contrast: Warm key light on the subject against a desaturated cool background; text in near-white with a 2px dark outline so it holds over both.
thumbnails.mobileReadability: Two text words only; at 168x94 px the face reads as a face and the arrow reads as direction. Squint test: subject silhouette and arrow survive, background detail does not — which is fine.

thumbnails.name: Artifact-led: show the thing itself
thumbnails.layout: The artifact fills the left 60% at a slight angle, text right-aligned in the remaining third, baseline centred vertically.
thumbnails.subject: The actual output of OpenClaw agents — the screen, doc, or board — cropped tight enough that one element is unambiguously readable.
thumbnails.emotion: Curiosity through specificity: it looks like a real screenshot, not a stock render.
thumbnails.contrast: Single bright accent (one highlighted row/box) against an otherwise muted frame; the accent is the only saturated colour in the image.
thumbnails.mobileReadability: One readable element plus two words. At thumbnail size the accent block is the anchor; everything else can blur without losing the message.

thumbnails.name: Before/after: the split frame
thumbnails.layout: Hard vertical split. Left panel = before state, right panel = after state, thin bright divider. Two-word label bottom-centre spanning the seam.
thumbnails.subject: Left: vague ideas. Right: finished workflows. Same framing on both sides so only the content changes.
thumbnails.emotion: Relief — the right panel is visibly calmer than the left.
thumbnails.contrast: Left panel cool and cluttered, right panel warm and clean; the divider is the brightest pixel in the frame.
thumbnails.mobileReadability: Composition reads before the text does, so it works even when the label is illegible. Keep each panel to one dominant shape.
